literal: Yanshen employed him; inscribed restraint ran very deep. Though his talent was without reproach, this too owed to Yanshen's introduction.
idiomatic: Zhao Yanshen took him up; Yuxiu remembered it with deep restraint. His talent needed no apology, yet even that owed to Yanshen's hand on the ladder.

literal: After he became Minister of Personnel, he held that he had won the post by public esteem.
idiomatic: Once he was Minister of Personnel, he believed he had earned the post by what the world thought of him.

literal: At first Feng Zicong as Vice Director concurrently handled selections; marriage alliances followed one upon another. Yuxiu often mocked him, telling people: "Master Feng arranges marriages and has not a spare day.
idiomatic: Earlier Feng Zicong, as vice director, had also run the selection office; wedding matches came one after another. Yuxiu often laughed at him and said to others, "Master Feng brokers marriages—his days have no spare hour."

literal: " When he himself held the selection office, he could not escape it either; opinion held it was the nature of the post.
idiomatic: " When he himself sat in that office, he could not escape the same; the talk of the time said it was the terrain of the post."

literal: In office he was honest and careful; few in his day could match him.
idiomatic: In office he was scrupulous and careful; few in his day could stand beside him.

literal: In Wei and Qi times, terrace gentlemen often could not avoid traffic in gifts and presents; Yuxiu spent ten years in the Masters of Writing and never once accepted so much as a cup of wine in tribute.
idiomatic: Under Wei and Qi, secretariat gentlemen seldom escaped gifts and favors; Yuxiu served ten years in the Masters of Writing and never took even a cup of wine as a gift.

literal: Minister Xing Shao and Yuxiu were old friends; in the ministry they would banter in jest and often called Yuxiu "Clear Gentleman."
idiomatic: Minister Xing Shao and Yuxiu were old intimates. In the ministry they traded jokes, and Shao often called Yuxiu "Clear Gentleman."

literal: In the first year of Daning, Yuxiu went out as Vice Director of the Grand Ceremonials on an inspection tour, and was also ordered to assess officials' merits and faults.
idiomatic: In the first Daning year, Yuxiu left the capital as vice director of the Grand Ceremonials on a circuit inspection, and was told to weigh officials' gains and failures.

literal: Passing through Yan Province, Xing Shao was then governor of Yan; after they parted, Shao sent white silk as a token.
idiomatic: His route took him through Yan province, where Xing Shao was governor. After they had parted, Shao sent white silk as a courtesy.

literal: Yuxiu returned the silk and would not accept it, writing to Xing: "Today I pass above—an unusual circumstance. 'Melon field, plum beneath'—the ancients were wary of it; many words bring fear, like holding back a river. I pray you take this heart and do not lay heavy blame on me.
idiomatic: Yuxiu sent the silk back and wrote Xing: "Today I pass through your ground—an uncommon walk. The ancients warned of the melon field and the plum tree; many words are to be feared, like a river you must bank. Take this as my heart, and do not lay a heavy charge on me."

literal: " Xing also gladly understood, replying: "A gift of a single day, offered without thought; this old man in his haste did not reach so far. I respectfully receive your meaning—between us there is no gap.
idiomatic: " Xing took it gladly and answered: "A gift of a single day, sent without thinking it through—this old man, in his haste, never got that far. I accept your meaning; between us there is no gap."

literal: You, younger brother, were once Clear Gentleman; today you are Clear Minister again.
idiomatic: " You were once Clear Gentleman; today you are Clear Minister again."

literal: When he was in the Ministry of Personnel, government was blocked and the Way was lost; to go against powerful interests would bring disaster in no time. Though he kept himself by integrity, he still could not escape the burden of petition visits.
idiomatic: In the Ministry of Personnel the age was corrupt; to cross those who mattered was to invite ruin overnight. He kept his hands clean, yet even so could not shake off the drag of callers bearing gifts.

literal: When Qi fell he entered Zhou, appointed Colonel-in-Ordinary of the First Rank and Vice Minister in the Ministry of Personnel.
idiomatic: When Qi fell he entered Zhou and was made colonel-in-ordinary of the first rank and vice minister in the Ministry of Personnel.

literal: Late in the Elephant reign he was made Director of the Imperial Clan at the Eastern Capital, vice minister.
idiomatic: Late in the Elephant reign he was made director of the imperial clan at the Eastern Capital, with vice-minister rank.

literal: At the opening of Sui Kaihuang he was given additional Grand Colonel-in-Ordinary of the First Rank and transferred to Minister of the Capital at the Eastern Capital.
idiomatic: When Sui opened under Kaihuang he was raised to grand colonel-in-ordinary of the first rank and moved to minister of the capital at the Eastern Capital.

literal: When the Eastern Capital was abolished he entered court and was again made Minister of Justice.
idiomatic: When the Eastern Capital was abolished he came to court and was again made Minister of Justice.

literal: In the second year he went out as governor of Xiong Province.
idiomatic: In the second year he went out as governor of Xiong province.

literal: Soon after he died, aged seventy-two.
idiomatic: Before long he died, at seventy-two.

literal: His son Zhi Li, late in Wuping, was Colonel-in-Ordinary and staff officer of an establishment that opened the government.
idiomatic: His son Zhi Li, late in Wuping, was colonel-in-ordinary and staff officer of an establishment that opened the government.

literal: Under Sui Kaihuang he was attendant censor, and served through Minister of the Household for the People and Vice Director of Merit Assessment.
idiomatic: Under Sui Kaihuang he was attendant censor, then passed through minister of the household for the people and vice director of merit assessment.

literal: Early in Daye he died in the post of Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
idiomatic: Early in Daye he died while serving as attendant of the heir apparent.

literal: The historiographer says: Cui Yanxuan bore virtue through generations and did not shame his forebears;
idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Cui Yanxuan carried virtue down the generations and did not disgrace his line;

literal: Lu the Chamberlain loved knights-errant and liked stratagems; his aims were broad and far;
idiomatic: Lu Qian, as chamberlain, loved bold companions and good counsel; his aims ran wide and long;

literal: Yang the Vice Director stood high in rank and heavy in esteem, flourishing as the age's pillar;
idiomatic: Yang Xiuzhi the vice director stood high in rank and weight in the world's eyes, a pillar of his time;

literal: Yuan the Minister was clear within himself and trusted for his capacity;
idiomatic: Yuan Yuxiu the minister kept clarity in his own person and was trusted for what he could do;

literal: together with Yang Fei and Lu Qian they were the court's fine men.
idiomatic: with Yang Fei and Lu Qian they were the court's best men.

literal: In Qi's late age power fell to flatterers; these gentlemen alone upheld name and teaching—otherwise roots would have been torn up and sources stopped, caps torn off and regalia destroyed; how could it be spoken of!
idiomatic: In Qi's last days power went to flatterers; only these men held up rites and learning. Without them the roots would have been pulled and the source dammed, caps torn off and regalia trampled—who could even name such an age?

literal: Appraisal: Only these several lords—hearts at ease with favor and disgrace, neither harsh nor indulgent—sat firm over the drifting manners of the age.
idiomatic: Praise: These men alone—hearts at ease with favor and disgrace, neither harsh nor soft—sat like weights on the age's drifting customs.

literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
idiomatic: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
